paper_title: Another Subexponential-time Quantum Algorithm for the Dihedral Hidden Subgroup Problem
source_locator: Explicit open question on PDF page 5
statement: All known subexponential algorithms for the hidden subgroup problems make no use of the output when the target set X is unstructured. (We do not know whether it is even possible to make good use of the output with only subexponentially many queries.) The best description of what happens is that the algorithm discards the output and leave the input register in a mixed state ρ. However, it is commonly said that the algorithm measures the output. This is a strange description if the algorithm then makes no use of the measurement; its sole virtue is that it leaves the quantum state of the input register in a pure state |ψi. The state |ψi is randomly chosen from a distribution, which is the same as saying that the register is in a mixed state ρ.
context: Uf |g, x0 i = |g, f (g) + x0 i. All known subexponential algorithms for the hidden subgroup problems make no use of the output when the target set X is unstructured. The best description of what happens is that the algorithm discards the output and leave the input register in a mixed state ρ. However, it is commonly said that the algorithm measures the output. This is a strange description if the algorithm then makes no use of the measurement; its sole virtue is that it leaves the quantum state of the input register in a pure state |ψi. The state |ψi is randomly chosen from a distribution, which is the same as saying that the register is in a mixed state ρ. If the output of f is always discarded, then the algorithm works just as well if the output of f is a state |ψ(g)i in a Hilbert space H. The injectivity condition is replaced by the orthogonality condition hψ(g)|ψ(h)i = 0 when g and h lie in distinct cosets of H.
